tool.name: Beacon2 Sequence Query
tool.description: find a precise variant at a genomic position across federated beacons
tool.command: #if str($connection.transport) == "api" beacon2-query sequence @PROVIDER_ARGS@ @VARIANT_CLASS_ARGS@ --reference-name '$reference_name' --assembly '$assembly' --start $start --reference-bases '$reference_bases' --alternate-bases '$alternate_bases' --granularity '$granularity' --limit $pagination.limit --skip $pagination.skip @SAMPLE_ARGS@ #if str($advanced.allow_coalescing) == "false" --no-coalescing #end if @SV_TERM_ARGS@ @CNV_TERM_ARGS@ @FILTER_ARGS@ @OUTPUT_ARGS@ #else beacon2-query sequence --transport mongodb --db-host '$connection.db_host' --db-port $connection.db_port --database '$connection.database' --collection '$connection.collection' --credentials-file '$credentials' --reference-name '$reference_name' --start $start --reference-bases '$reference_bases' --alternate-bases '$alternate_bases' @OUTPUT_ARGS@ #end if

param.label: Position
param.help: 1-based, as you would read it in a genome browser or a paper. Converted internally to the 0-based coordinates the API uses.

param.label: Reference bases
param.help: The base or bases present in the reference at this position, e.g. G.

validator.message: Use A, C, G, T or N only

param.label: Alternate bases
param.help: The base or bases you are looking for, e.g. A. N acts as a wildcard: ANNT matches ACGT, ACCT and so on.

validator.message: Use A, C, G, T or N only

param.name: allow_coalescing
param.label: Combine identical queries across variant classes
param.help: When two classes would produce exactly the same request, send it once and sort the results afterwards. The combined result is only used if the beacon reports a complete, exact count; otherwise each class is queried separately. Turn this off to always query each class independently.

tool.help:
**What it does**
@HELP_READS@
Looks for a precise variant at a single position — the classic Beacon question, "do you have anyone with this change?" This is the tool for SNVs and short insertions or deletions, where you know the reference base or bases and the alternate you are looking for.
For anything defined by a region rather than a position, use the Range Query tool. For copy number and structural variants with imprecise breakpoints, use the Bracket Query tool.
**Worked example: a single base change in EIF4A1**
::
Chromosome: 17 Position: 7,577,120 Reference bases: G Alternate bases: A
Enter the position as you would read it in a genome browser. The tool converts to the 0-based coordinates the API expects, so you never have to adjust by one.
**Wildcards**
``N`` matches any base, in either field. An alternate of ``ANNT`` matches ``ACGT``, ``ACCT``, ``AGGT`` and so on, which is useful when you care about the flanking bases but not the middle.
@HELP_VARIANT_CLASS@
**Combining identical queries**
If you select more than one variant class and the resulting requests would be identical, the tool sends one request and sorts the results by class afterwards — but only keeps that shortcut when the beacon reports a complete and exact count for the query. If anything was truncated, or the count is approximate, each class is queried separately instead and the report says so. The saving never comes at the cost of a weaker claim about what was found.
@HELP_VARIANT_SIZE@
@HELP_DEGRADATION@
@HELP_OUTPUTS@
**Credentials**
Public beacons need none. For registered or controlled beacons, set the relevant key under *User → Preferences → Manage information*. A missing credential is reported per beacon as ``auth_missing``, naming the preference key to set — the tool never echoes the value itself.
